facts.detail: Customers should first contact the provider's customer-services department and explain the problem.
If initial contact does not resolve the problem, the customer should make a formal complaint using details on the bill, provider website or customer services.
Phone and broadband companies must maintain an easily accessible complaints code of practice.
Providers must take prompt and active steps to resolve complaints and promptly communicate the outcome.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint-handling rights do not prove network coverage, speed or orderability at a parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom ADR schemes and phone-provider problem guide

facts.detail: Unresolved phone or broadband complaints can be referred to an independent ADR scheme free of charge.
Eligibility includes residential customers, small businesses with up to 10 employees and qualifying not-for-profit organisations.
Referral is available after six weeks or earlier with a deadlock letter when agreement cannot be reached.
The current Ofcom guide requires referral within 12 months of receiving a deadlock letter.

guard_streams.write_limit: ADR eligibility and remedies are consumer-protection evidence, not parcel service evidence.

facts.detail: Customers can text INFO to 85075 to check contract status and possible early termination charges.
Customers keeping their number can text PAC to 65075.
Customers taking a new number can text STAC to 75075.
The provider must normally return the PAC or STAC within one minute and the code is valid for 30 days.

guard_streams.write_limit: Text-to-Switch codes and contract information do not establish mobile coverage at an address.

facts.detail: After receiving the PAC or STAC, the new provider must complete the switch within one working day.
The old provider must not charge for a notice period after the switching date.
Service loss must not exceed one working day and compensation is required when switching goes wrong.
A cancelled customer can request free number retention within one month of cancellation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching times and compensation do not prove current signal or parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new provider and that provider arranges the broadband switch.
The process tells the customer about applicable early termination charges.
The customer provides the services to switch, address and current-provider name.
Once the new service is working, the old broadband service ends automatically.

guard_streams.write_limit: Broadband switching workflow is not exact parcel availability or measured-speed evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom scam-call text and message action guide

facts.detail: Consumers should not reply, click links, press buttons or share personal or financial details with suspicious contacts.
Consumers should hang up and avoid calling back unfamiliar numbers, especially premium-rate ranges.
Suspected scam calls or SMS messages can be reported to 7726 free of charge.
A claimed organisation should be called back using a number from its official website or account statement, not a number supplied by the caller.

guard_streams.write_limit: Scam-safety advice and reports do not identify network coverage or parcel performance.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom tackling scam calls from abroad statement

facts.detail: Providers are expected to identify and block calls from abroad that spoof UK landline numbers.
The 2024 CLI guidance expects blocking of foreign calls using a UK Presentation Number except limited legitimate cases.
The July 2026 update covers calls from abroad presenting UK mobile +447 numbers.
Where validity cannot be verified, the spoofed UK mobile Presentation Number will appear withheld to the recipient.

guard_streams.write_limit: CLI and spoofing controls are anti-fraud measures, not exact address connectivity evidence.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 38,000 premises for £71 million and was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 36,000 premises backed by up to £76.4 million.
The redesign followed commercial rollout expansion and market change to reduce overlap.
Detailed planning and physical build precede service and the premise list remains subject to change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract redesign totals do not establish current parcel orderability.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre Suffolk contract covered around 79,500 premises for £100.5 million and was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 60,000 premises backed by up to £118.2 million.
The redesign focuses public funding on premises outside expanded commercial rollout.
Trenching, ducts and fibre installation precede access, and detailed planning can change the scope.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional redesign and planned construction are not parcel delivery evidence.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre Norfolk contract covered around 62,200 premises for £114.2 million and was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 33,000 premises backed by £61.9 million.
The redesign reduces commercial overlap and focuses subsidy on premises otherwise missed.
Planning and physical build precede service and technical findings may change the premise list.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract values and revised scope cannot prove live parcel service.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre Hampshire contract covered around 75,500 premises for £104.2 million and was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 29,000 premises backed by £71.7 million.
Commercial rollout expansion and market conditions drove the reduced public scope.
Detailed plans and construction are required before service and the premise list may change.

guard_streams.write_limit: A redesigned contract is procurement evidence, not exact parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract targeted around 52,000 premises across East and West Sussex.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 13,000 premises backed by £25.2 million.
The redesign followed substantial commercial expansion and changing market conditions.
Supplier discussions and planning status do not identify which exact parcels are delivered.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional contract scope and supplier discussions cannot populate exact parcel rows.

facts.detail: Freedom Fibre was awarded a contract in November 2023 to reach 12,000 North Shropshire premises.
The update records 2,500 premises built and a further 1,000 targeted by the end of June 2025.
BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually agreed to descope the remaining 8,500 premises.
In April 2026, premises in the area were added to Openreach call-off three.

guard_streams.write_limit: Partial delivery, descope and reassignment do not establish exact parcel completion.

facts.detail: The July table records Sussex at 12,760 contracted and 3,020 built, and Hampshire at 29,420 contracted and 7,150 built.
Leicestershire and Warwickshire is recorded at 22,480 contracted and 10,740 built.
Norfolk is recorded at 32,670 contracted and 13,310 built, while Suffolk is 38,350 contracted and 18,560 built.
The data is a rounded snapshot with ingestion lag and must not be used to assess contractual milestones.
